metadata.note: The Connecticut and Passumpsic Rivers Railroad (chartered 1835, revived 1843, built 1847-1867) and the corridor's later operators: White River Junction - Wells River - St. Johnsbury - Newport, VT and, over the leased Massawippi Valley Railway, on to Lennoxville, PQ. One feature per drawable section x operator (Rule 4 splits at the 1887 Boston and Maine lease, the 1926 Canadian Pacific takeover north of Wells River and the 1 Jun 1926 Quebec Central sub-lease of the Massawippi). Features covering the same section share identical geometry. Drawn from research/branches/connecticut_and_passumpsic_rivers_railroad.txt (researched 2026-10-15); only its drawable spans are drawn.
sources: Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 (schedules eff. 30 Sep 1951): CP Table 11 'Montreal, Newport, Wells River and Boston' with times, and the station index (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt)
ICC, 30 Val. Rep. 515 (1930), Valuation Docket 221 - NOT read directly; quoted via the Wikipedia Massawippi Valley Railway article
Bradford, VT town history, via research/branches/bradford_railroad.txt block [2] (opening to Bradford 10 Oct 1848)
not_yet_sourced: [OPEN] Quebec Central Newport - Lennoxville passenger end: drawn to 1951 (last confirmed year, Wikipedia 'Connecticut Yankee' citing NH timetables); the true end lies 1951-1960 (Wikipedia 'Massawippi Valley Railway' says 'entirely by 1960'). A QC timetable of 1953-59 or the Dec 1954 Official Guide QC section would settle it.
[OPEN] Stanstead branch: opening year unknown (drawn from 1894, earliest RPO postmark); Quebec Central Beebe Jct - Rock Island end unknown (drawn to 1936, last Fowler letter).
[ANCHOR] Green Mountain Railroad White River Flyer: only 2010 is proven.

The 1887 takeover: leased 1 Jan 1887 (Boston and Lowell system) vs B&M via the 1 Apr 1887 Boston and Lowell lease vs 'Connecticut River RR 1887' vs Dartmouth's '1877' vs VTT's '1893'. B&M-system operation from 1887 is drawn; the formal lessee is unsettled.
Wells River - Newport transfer to CP: 1925 (Fowler) vs 1926 (VTT; first Alouette over CP 26 Apr 1926). Drawn B&M to 1925, CP from 1926.
Wells River - St. Johnsbury opening: Nov 1850 (St. Johnsbury History & Heritage Center) vs 1851 (unread secondary); drawn from 1851.
St. Johnsbury - Barton: track 1858, first train reported 1863; drawn from 1863.
Newport - border: reached May 1867 (VTT, ICC) vs 'Derby Line by 1863' (Dartmouth); whether trains ran to the border 1867-1869 is unproven; drawn from 1870 (Massawippi Valley opening).
Massawippi lessee 1887-1919: B&M assumed the lease in 1887 (RPO) vs C&P operated it to 1919 (Wikipedia).
Headways and speeds are estimates throughout; the only counted frequency is Sept 1951 (3 trains each way Wells River - Newport, OG52 CP Table 11).
Chronicling America full text was unreachable during research; opening-day and last-train newspaper reports remain unchecked.

metadata.freight_only_note: Not drawn (freight only): Wells River - Newport after 30 Oct 1965 and White River Junction - Wells River after Apr 1965 (CP, B&M, later Washington County RR freight); the Massawippi line after the withheld passenger end (freight to 1990, rails lifted 1992); the private 'Passumpsic Railroad' heritage operation at Barnet (no public passenger service established).

segments.note: B&M operation from 1887: the C&P was leased into the Boston and Lowell system from 1 Jan 1887 and the B&M leased the Boston and Lowell on 1 Apr 1887 (WP-BM), running the line as the Passumpsic Division. The 1946 sale of this section to the B&M changed title, not operator. Carried Springfield / New York - Quebec trains (Connecticut Yankee from 1936) and Boston connections at White River Junction; from late 1954 the Boston - Montreal Alouette and Red Wing were rerouted over this section (until then they reached Wells River via Plymouth and Woodsville), with unnamed RDCs #31/32 from 1956. Ends 1965: the B&M withdrew from the Boston - Montreal pool from 25 Apr 1965 (Wikipedia 'Alouette', citing Holland 2004). Freight continued afterwards (later Washington County RR / Vermont Rail System) - context only. Other dates for the takeover (1877, 1893) are recorded in metadata.not_yet_sourced. headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates, not taken from a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: start from WP-BM (1 Apr 1887 Boston and Lowell lease) and NCS (C&P operations 1848-1887); end from WP-AL (B&M out of the pool 25 Apr 1965); Fowler section 1 letter d (1953 B&M public timetable) at every station; OG52 index lists Bradford on B&M table 16 (times not recovered).

segments.note: CP's Lyndonville Subdivision, Wells River - St. Johnsbury - Lyndonville - Barton - Newport. CP took over in 1926: the first Boston - Montreal Alouette ran 26 Apr 1926 'over Canadian Pacific trackage to Wells River' (WP-AL; VTT 1926; Fowler says 1925). CP leased the line in 1926 and bought it in 1946 - a change of title, not operator. Carried the Alouette and Red Wing (to 24 Oct 1959) and the Connecticut Yankee's Wells River - Newport leg; through trains continued from Newport to Montreal over CP's own North Troy - Richford line (not drawn here). The Feb 1952 Official Guide's CP Table 11 (eff. 30 Sep 1951) shows three trains each way with times - the only frequency actually counted, for 1951. Ends 1965: after the B&M left the pool on 25 Apr 1965 CP ran #31/32 Montreal - Wells River alone until 30 Oct 1965 (WP-AL). A 1967 CP employee timetable for the subdivision is freight evidence only; freight continued (later Washington County RR) - context only. headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates, not taken from a timetable.

segments.note: Quebec Central (CP-leased since 1912/13 but operated as a distinct company) sub-leased the Massawippi Valley and the Newport - border line from the B&M on 1 Jun 1926 (BNAPS RPO newsletter; WP-MV citing Mundy's 1927). Quebec - Sherbrooke - Newport trains connecting with B&M/CP at Newport; Connecticut Yankee through sleepers from 1936 (WP-CY citing B&M 1937/1946, CP 1943 and OG Aug 1949 timetables); 'Newport & Sherbrooke' RPO postmarks 1929-1941. [OPEN] END: 1951 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end. Wikipedia 'Connecticut Yankee' (citing the NH timetable of 29 Apr 1951) is the latest positive evidence of rail passenger service; it then says the route ended at Wells River with a bus to Sherbrooke from between summer 1951 and autumn 1952, while Wikipedia 'Massawippi Valley Railway' (from a dead r2parks.net page) says the runs ended 'entirely by 1960'. Fowler has these stations in the 1936 Canadian Guide but not the 1958 QC timetable. No source dates when service actually stopped. Do not extend without evidence. Freight continued to 1990 - context only. headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates, not taken from a timetable.

properties.review_open: Two decisions left to the reviewer: (1) whether the Quebec Central should keep its own colour or fold into Canadian Pacific's (Rule 4 tracks who ran the trains, and the QC operated as a distinct unit under its CP lease, so it is drawn as its own company here); (2) Rule 9 scope - this feature is mostly in Quebec and run by a Canadian company, kept only because it served Newport, VT and continues a US road's route.

Ends 1925: the 1925 B&M timetable is the last that shows Stanstead itself (Fowler); the B&M era ended with the Quebec Central sub-lease of 1 Jun 1926, and the Beebe Jct - Rock Island part may have carried B&M trains into 1926 - not drawn. headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates, not taken from a timetable.

properties.line: Quebec Central: Beebe Junction – Rock Island
properties.speed_source: estimate; no schedule speed was sourced for this section (research report UNRESOLVED 9)
properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap (Overpass) with opstrace.py, except as stated. Traced vs documented: Beebe Junction - Rock Island 2.4 mi traced (no separate documented figure; whole spur 3.4 mi Fowler / 2.4 mi Wikipedia). Stanstead branch: from the junction vertex, the OSM way 'Stanstead Branch Line' (old_railway_operator=Quebec Central Railway) and the untagged abandoned-railway cycleway 'Piste Cyclable de Stanstead' east along the border to Rock Island, then the abandoned-railway cycleway north into Stanstead. ONE STRAIGHT-LINE LEG, approximated: 0.33 mi across an unmapped gap at Rock Island (45.0071 N 72.1134 W to 45.0077 N 72.1066 W). The Rock Island split point is the bend where the grade turns north, not a surveyed station site. Alignment caveat: the trace is the right-of-way as it survives (the 20th-century alignment, partly a rail-trail); no 19th-century relocation was checked, so for C&P-era features this may be a later alignment than the era drawn.

segments.note: Quebec Central era of the Stanstead spur, from the 1 Jun 1926 sub-lease (RPO). By 1936 Rock Island was the terminus (Fowler: Rock Island carries the 1936 Canadian Guide letter as a terminus; Stanstead does not), so only Beebe Junction - Rock Island is drawn. Sherbrooke & Stanstead RPO postmarks run to 17 Jun 1929. [OPEN] END: 1936 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when service stopped. Do not extend without evidence. headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates, not taken from a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: start from RPO (QC sub-lease 1 Jun 1926); end [OPEN] from Fowler PQ section 92 letter c (1936 Canadian Guide, Rock Island terminus).

properties.line: Green Mountain Railroad: White River Flyer (White River Junction – Thetford)
properties.speed_source: estimate for a slow excursion train; not sourced
properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap (Overpass): the active Washington County Railroad Connecticut River and Lyndonville Subdivisions (old_railway_operator=CP / B&M) south of Newport, the CP-tagged Newport Bike Path and Beebe Spur rail-trail Newport - Beebe, and the Massawippi Valley rail-trails (Sentier Nature Tomifobia, Axe de la Massawippi, old_railway_operator 'Canadian Pacific Railway;Massawippi Valley Railway') north to Lennoxville. Routed with opstrace.py (Douglas-Peucker 8 m, trim_reversals); 99% of the traced length is on ways tagged for this road's later operators, the rest short untagged connecting rail; no straight-line leg. Traced vs documented: White River Junction - Thetford 13.8 mi traced vs 14.1 mi (Fowler MP 123.1-137.2). Same rails as the C&P / B&M White River Junction - Wells River features, cut at Thetford (East Thetford). Alignment caveat: the trace is the right-of-way as it survives (the 20th-century alignment, partly a rail-trail); no 19th-century relocation was checked, so for C&P-era features this may be a later alignment than the era drawn.

segments.note: Seasonal 'White River Flyer' excursions over the old C&P main line from White River Junction via Norwich (Montshire Museum of Science stop) to Thetford, run by the Green Mountain Railroad (Vermont Rail System). [ANCHOR]: 2010 is the one proven year (Fowler's letter h, 'Vermont Rly (VR), tourist line 2010', at WRJ, Montshire Museum and Thetford). Service certainly ran wider both ways - a Jan 2010 forum post calls the train 'recently established' and the Wikipedia White River Junction station article describes the excursions in the present tense - but no other year is confirmed. Do not widen without evidence. Counts as passenger service under Rule 1. headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates, not taken from a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: 2010 from Fowler section 1 letter h; WP-WRJ for the operation (undated).
